provenance: M8 sixth tranche: every far record of Ibn Rajab's qawāʿid 35, 37, 38, 39 and 41, annotated against readings formalised from each qāʿida's own statement (Usul.Refinements). Annotated by reading the full paragraph in the pinned witness; every claim of agreement is guarded by Lean (UsulTest/Takhrij.lean); classes and facts await human review (Review.tla).

positions.who: the ṣaḥīḥ (al-Qāḍī, Ibn ʿAqīl, most): the lease stands
wajh: dissolved, as with buying the wife

cases.note: The lessee buys the leased thing from its lessor: two wujūh (or riwāyas); «والثاني: لا ينفسخ وهو الصحيح وهو اختيار القاضي وابن عقيل والأكثرين», the benefits having left the lessor first. A marriage, by contrast, dissolves on buying the wife.

positions.who: al-Qāḍī's Khilāf, the madhhab: not dissolved

cases.note: Renting a house from his father, then inheriting it: two wujūh (al-Talkhīṣ derives them from the previous farʿ); «والمذهب عند القاضي في الخلاف أنه لا ينفسخ»; al-Mujarrad: dissolved, inheritance being compulsory.
Buying an unpollinated spathe on condition of cutting («بشرط قطعه»), then its palm: «والمجزوم به في الكافي أنه لا ينفسخ بغير خلاف», though Ibn Rajab notes hesitation since it follows in sale.

positions.who: al-Qāḍī, Ibn ʿAqīl, al-Mughnī: liable as a loan
Majd al-Dīn, ẓāhir of Aḥmad: never liable

cases.note: A pledge, then permission to use it: does it become a loan while used? al-Qāḍī, Ibn ʿAqīl, al-Mughnī, al-Talkhīṣ: liable by use, «لأن ذلك حقيقة العارية»; Majd al-Dīn: «ظاهر كلام أحمد أنه لا يصير مضمونا بحال». Reconciled (jamʿ, the binding farq of f003): the pledge binds (lāzim) and the permission does not, so it stays a pledge; the reading now takes Majd's ẓāhir of Aḥmad.

positions.who: al-Qāḍī, Ibn ʿAqīl: liable while used
later authors, ẓāhir of Aḥmad: not liable

cases.note: A deposit, then permission to use it: al-Qāḍī, Ibn ʿAqīl, al-Talkhīṣ: liable while used, «لمصيره عارية»; some later authors: the ẓāhir of Aḥmad is that it is not, as with the pledge. Under the binding refinement it stays liable (deposit and loan are alike non-binding (jāʾiz), «ولا اختلاف هاهنا بين العقدين في الجواز»; Majd distinguishes it from the pledge), which leaves it a residue against the later authors' ẓāhir.

Lending a thing to be pledged: valid by naṣṣ, with Ibn al-Mundhir's report of agreement; liable on the pledger as borrower, a trust with the pledgee. Whether it binds the owner (its luzūm) is disputed (al-Ḥārithī, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb).
Lending a thing, then pledging it with the borrower: Abū al-Barakāt, «قياس المذهب صحته ويسقط ضمان العارية», the binding (lāzim) trust displacing the non-binding loan.

A pledge contracted on usurped goods: «فيصح عندنا … ويبرأ به الغاصب» (Abū Bakr, al-Qāḍī), and likewise deposit, loan or hire to it (Abū al-Khaṭṭāb); al-Qāḍī gives two wujūh for hire, and for muḍāraba clears him only on spending.
Pledging the sold thing, still at the seller's risk, before delivery: if valid, the risk lapses, «لأن يده صارت يد ارتهان».

positions.who: al-Qāḍī, Ibn ʿAqīl: liable after the time
Aḥmad (Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Hārūn): never liable

cases.note: «If I bring your due by such a time, else the pledge is yours»: a trust until then, then liable, the hold being by a fāsid contract (al-Qāḍī, Ibn ʿAqīl); a riwāya of Aḥmad: never liable, the void condition («الشرط يفسد») counting as absent. Reconciled (jamʿ): the void sale binds nothing and does not displace the binding (lāzim) pledge; the reading now takes the riwāya of Aḥmad.

positions.who: wajh: the heirs', under the tadbīr

cases.note: Kitāba of a mudabbar, or tadbīr of a mukātab: valid by naṣṣ; if the master dies before any payment he is freed by tadbīr from the third, and his earnings are his (as a mukātab) or the heirs' on two wujūh; Ibn al-Ḥakam's narration has kitāba voiding the tadbīr («بطلان التدبير بالكتابة»).

positions.who: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, al-Qāḍī: valid, read by its meaning
Abū al-Khaṭṭāb elsewhere, as the madhhab: void

cases.note: A loan of use with a countervalue stipulated («وشرط عليه العوض»): valid as a kināya for qarḍ (Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, al-Qāḍī; the countervalue as in a gift); or fāsid, «وجعله أبو الخطاب في موضع آخر المذهب».

«Take this as muḍāraba, all the profit yours (or mine)»: al-Qāḍī, Ibn ʿAqīl: a fāsid muḍāraba with the usual wage; al-Mughnī elsewhere: a valid ibḍāʿ, «فراعى الحكم دون اللفظ», and a loan in the first form. No madhhab marked.
Hiring measured goods or money without stating a use: al-Qāḍī: valid, as a loan; another wajh: not valid. No madhhab marked.
Leasing land for a third of its crop: valid by Aḥmad's naṣṣ; the aṣḥāb dispute its meaning (al-Qāḍī: a lease like muzāraʿa; Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, Ibn ʿAqīl, al-Mughnī: muzāraʿa under the word of lease).
Salam in something present: valid as a sale, or not? «وهو ظاهر كلام أحمد في رواية المروذي لا يصح البيع بلفظ السلم»; al-Qāḍī in one place: valid.

positions.who: riwāya: divorce (ṭalāq, «أعني به الطلاق»), as he meant

cases.note: «You are ḥarām to me, I mean divorce», ḥarām being explicit for ẓihār: is the explanation set aside («يلغو») and it ẓihār, or valid («يصح») and divorce? Two riwāyas. No madhhab marked.

«Settle the salam debt with me for the like of the price»: al-Qāḍī: valid as iqāla; he and Ibn ʿAqīl: selling the debt to the debtor for its like is not allowed, «فيخرج في المسألة وجهان التفاتا إلى اللفظ والمعنى».
Leasing a thing with the word «sale»: two wujūh; al-Talkhīṣ: not valid if the sale is added to the thing, the two wujūh being where it is added to the benefit. No madhhab marked.

positions.who: wajh: valid where no witnessing is required

cases.note: Taking back a wife (rajʿa) by allusion: not valid if witnessing is required, otherwise two wujūh (al-Targhīb), «والأولى ما ذكرناه». In the same paragraph, «I free you and make your freedom your ṣadāq»: Ibn Ḥāmid: an allusion that does not conclude a marriage; al-Qāḍī: explicit; and Aḥmad's own words make it an allusion valid with intention, against the nikāḥ exception.

positions.who: ẓāhir of the aṣḥāb, al-Qāḍī: a pledge on taking
al-Kāfī, al-Talkhīṣ, Abū al-Khaṭṭāb: needs the pledger

cases.note: A pledge destroyed and its value taken: «فظاهر كلامهم أنها تكون رهنا بمجرد الأخذ», so al-Qāḍī lets the agent sell the substitute without new permission; al-Kāfī and al-Talkhīṣ disagree, and Abū al-Khaṭṭāb's ẓāhir needs the pledger to make it a pledge.
A waqf destroyed, its value used to buy a replacement: is it waqf without the administrator making it so? Two wujūh. No madhhab marked.
A designated sacrifice destroyed (or sold by its designator), its like bought with the value: designated by the purchase itself? Derived on two wujūh. No madhhab marked.
A bequeathed thing destroyed after the death and before acceptance: «فحقه باق في بدلها».
